findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_nav_icon_rail.rs:53-56 and :818 owed_destinations, consumed by :865 assert_rail_offers; acceptance row 'nav-collapse-icon-rail.feature P4 obligations L5/F107,L5/F108,L5/F109,L5/F110'
findings.obligation: P4 and L5: with the nav folded, every member including Teams, Invite a member and Machine tokens is in the layout, visible, focusable and named by its own word, and at 480px and below no page slides sideways. The acceptance row disposes this as Tested by RE-RUNNING the shipped nav-collapse-icon-rail lane unchanged.
findings.observation: The shipped lane does not quantify over the members it reads. Only the OFFERED set comes from the live document (support/rail_reading.rs:74); the EXPECTED set is built at feature_nav_icon_rail.rs:818 from the hardcoded constants at :53-56 - EVERY_OPERATOR = [Home, Board, Settings, Keyboard shortcuts], plus Integrations and Instance admin by rights, plus Sign out - and :865 compares the two with a sorted assert_eq, i.e. set EQUALITY. Once the three new members are authored inside nav#sidebar-nav, every rail scenario that calls assert_rail_offers (nav-collapse-icon-rail.feature:62, :82, :170 and the lane's sibling rows) fails with 'the rail announces [... Invite a member, Machine tokens, Teams ...] where her rights give her [Board, Home, Keyboard shortcuts, Settings, Sign out]'. That failure is the inverse of P1, exactly like the Slice-09 guard this slice correctly migrated, and neither feature_nav_icon_rail.rs nor nav-collapse-icon-rail.feature appears in the slice's changed-file selection. Consequence: P4 has no usable falsifier for the enlarged set, and the crafter inherits a red oracle it may not edit (production steps never edit oracle files).
findings.remediation: Before craft, migrate the lane that the acceptance row claims as P4's falsifier: make owed_destinations derive the owed set from the destinations the OPEN nav offers her (the same document the rail reading already parses), or add Teams, Invite a member and Machine tokens to EVERY_OPERATOR so the owed set names the five primary members, Settings, Keyboard shortcuts, the two gated members and Sign out. Then restate the acceptance row for L5/F107-F110 as Migrated rather than unchanged-and-Tested, and keep the lane run with FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=nav-collapse-icon-rail FOUNDRY_XTASK_INCLUDE_DOCKER=1 as P4's completion obligation.

Durable facts read from it: argv 'cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --test acceptance' (nav-quick-actions feature), release build finished, summary '10 scenarios (2 passed, 8 failed), 61 steps (53 passed, 8 failed)', harness exit non-zero with 'acceptance run failed: 8 step(s) failed, 0 parsing error(s), 0 hook error(s)'.

The measured RED is semantic, not BROKEN: zero parsing errors and zero hook errors, every Given and every When passed, and all 8 failures are business assertions on the missing behaviour. Five scenarios fail on 'the left nav must offer [Home /, Board <board>, Teams /teams, Invite a member /workspace/invites, Machine tokens /admin/tokens] ... it offers [(Home,/),(Board,<board>)]'; three fail on 'the landing page still heads a "Quick actions" section; its headings are [Foundry, Your projects, Quick actions]'. No import, collection, dependency, fixture or cross-root failure appears. The two passing scenarios are the current-page outline on /teams and /account/settings, which pins already-satisfied behaviour (L6) and needs no RED.

P4's claimed inherited falsifier does not hold as the shipped lane stands. The design records 'P4 is inherited, not re-oracled ... covered by RE-RUNNING that lane', and the acceptance row lists nav-collapse-icon-rail.feature as Tested for L5/F107-F110 with no change. Read of that lane's support: crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_nav_icon_rail.rs:818 owed_destinations builds the EXPECTED set from hardcoded constants at :53-56 (EVERY_OPERATOR = [Home, Board, Settings, Keyboard shortcuts], plus Integrations/Instance admin by rights, plus Sign out), and :865 assert_rail_offers compares the names read from the live document against that set with sorted assert_eq (set EQUALITY, not containment). Only the OFFERED side is read from the document (support/rail_reading.rs:74), so once Teams, Invite a member and Machine tokens are authored every rail scenario using that helper fails with offered superset of wanted.

Survey of every other shipped consumer that enumerates sidebar members, to find further incompatible oracles: feature_navigation_bar.rs:77 primary_items plus :231 asserts containment ('must show a primary item'), and :288 counts only [aria-current=page] inside .sidebar__nav, so both survive five members; support/integrations_wayfinding.rs:443 then_sidebar_lists reads '.sidebar__user a' only, so the new nav members are outside its population; feature_nav_collapse.rs:1445 takes the first item only; feature_pwa_mobile.rs:548 measures links[0] and links[1] (Home, Board) on one row and asserts no count. feature_nav_icon_rail.rs is the only incompatible consumer found. Residue, not a finding: the pwa row could in principle be disturbed if wrapping moved Board off Home's row at phone width; no observation of that exists either way.

The two declared Migrated oracles are migrated completely and non-vacuously. navigation-bar-linear-ui.feature:189-200 keeps the reachability guard (body contains a link to /workspace/invites and /admin/tokens from /) and drops only the two inverse-of-P1 rows, with the superseded scope recorded in the comment; the retired step definition at feature_navigation_bar.rs:390 is now unreferenced, which cucumber-rs tolerates. canzan-theme-system.feature:203 and feature_canzan_theme.rs:775 drop the six .actions colour rows and rename the Then clause; eight dark-palette rows on .card, .card a and the section labels remain, so the scenario still measures something. A repository-wide grep for '.actions' in crates/foundry-acceptance now returns exactly one hit: the new negative assertion html::assert_not_has(body, 'ul.actions') at feature_nav_quick_actions.rs:242. No other consumer of the deleted markup survives.

Constructibility of the new scaffolding is established by execution, not by reading: both new Givens in feature_nav_quick_actions.rs ('Mei is on the team that owns the board' at :81 and 'Mei has since been made an instance super-admin' at :109) passed in the reused run for scenarios 2 and 3, which failed only at their Then. They seed through the same real Postgres and the shipped grant_instance_admin. The display name the reused persona writes is the first name itself (feature_dashboard_enhancements.rs:353 binds member_first_name to display_name), so 'the landing page still greets "Mei"' is satisfiable, and dashboard_root.html renders .dash__welcome, .dash__workspace and the h2 'Your projects' outside the section match, so all three landing-page scenarios including the NoTeam row are constructible once Quick actions is deleted.

Closure for P1, P2, P3 and the examiner expectations they carry is complete and each direction holds. P1/E2: the ordered (word, href) equality on nav#sidebar-nav a.sidebar__item refuses a member placed before Board, outside the nav or pointing elsewhere, and is read on a board page and on / with the fallback board href, so E2's order concern has a falsifier rather than a containment check. P1/P4 shape (L4): the icon-and-word step refuses zero or two glyphs, zero or two labels, a label unequal to the member's whole text, a <title> and an aria-label anywhere in the member. P2/E3,E5: no h1-h3 reads 'Quick actions' and no ul.actions, across the three publicly constructible landing states, while the greeting, the workspace line, the projects section and the project card are each asserted, so a removal that took too much fails. P3/E6,E7: the four rights rows are the whole domain of the two boolean rights facts, each asserting all five primary members plus user-menu containment for Integrations and Instance admin, so neither a new condition on the three nor a lost gate on the two can pass. L6: exactly one primary member marked, and it is Home, on /teams and /account/settings. No oracle observation lacks a declared obligation.

diagnostic: REJECTED for one concrete, phase-invalidating oracle defect; everything else in the candidate closes. P1, P2 and P3 have a constructible, public, independent oracle driven only through HTTP GET on the running binary with a real session and real Postgres, and their RED is measured and semantic: 8 of 10 scenarios fail on business assertions (the nav offers two of five promised destinations; the landing page still heads 'Quick actions'), with 0 parsing errors, 0 hook errors and every Given and When passing, so no BROKEN state masquerades as RED. The four rights rows exhaust the two-boolean rights domain; the landing-page kept-state assertions refuse an over-wide removal; the ordered (word, href) equality refuses a misplaced or mispointed member; L6 is already satisfied and stays green, which needs no RED.
